hints: Use integration by parts because the integrand is the product of \(x\) and \(\sec^2x\).
Take \(u=x\) and \(dv=\sec^2x\,dx\), giving an integral involving \(\tan x\).
Use \(\int\tan x\,dx=-\ln(\cos x)\), then evaluate the complete antiderivative at \(\pi/3\) and \(\pi/6\) and combine the logarithms exactly.
walkthrough:
State the definite integral to be evaluated:
$$I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} x\sec^2x\,dx$$

Apply integration by parts using the formula $\int u \dfrac{dv}{dx}\,dx = uv - \int v \dfrac{du}{dx}\,dx$:
Let $u = x \implies \dfrac{du}{dx} = 1$.
Let $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \sec^2x \implies v = \int \sec^2x\,dx = \tan x$.

Express the indefinite integral in terms of $u$ and $v$:
$$\int x\sec^2x\,dx = x\tan x - \int 1 \cdot \tan x\,dx = x\tan x - \int \tan x\,dx$$

Integrate $\tan x$ using the standard integral $\int \tan x\,dx = -\ln|\cos x| = \ln|\sec x|$:
$$\int x\sec^2x\,dx = x\tan x - (-\ln|\cos x|) = x\tan x + \ln|\cos x|$$

Set up the evaluation with the limits $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$:
$$I = \left[ x\tan x + \ln(\cos x) \right]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}$$

Evaluate the upper limit expression at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}$$
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Upper limit value} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\sqrt{3} + \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{3} - \ln 2$$

Evaluate the lower limit expression at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$:
$$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$$
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$
$$\text{Lower limit value} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right) + \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{18} + \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$I = \left( \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{3} + \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \right) - \left( \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{18} + \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \right)$$

Group and simplify the terms involving $\pi\sqrt{3}$:
$$\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{3} - \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{18} = \left(\dfrac{6}{18} - \dfrac{1}{18}\right)\pi\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{5\pi\sqrt{3}}{18}$$

Group and simplify the logarithmic terms using laws of logarithms:
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \ln\left( \dfrac{1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2} \right) = \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \ln\left(3^{-1/2}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\ln 3$$

Combine the simplified components to obtain the final exact value:
$$I = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}\,\pi}{18} - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln 3 \quad \left(\text{or } \dfrac{5\pi}{6\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln 3\right)$$
